-- F-75 **The compiled checker checks the Return Type Rule over every instance, and a positional rule: when two generic declarations in the more-specific relation declare as many static parameters of their own, those parameters agree in kind by position, and the more specific return type is a subtype of the other once the other's parameters are read as its own by position.** The equal-count scope and the comparison of kinds are the rung's choices. It builds P-45. Checking every instance, as P-45 asks, it also refuses a generic declaration beside a plain one whose domain is an object type, a pair that the type group's 2011 paper (`Papers/Types/`) accepts, since the paper sets aside the instances whose domains cannot meet (row 542, open). In the interpreter's library the two rules refuse no pair: the distance holds no return-type or overloading error (F-53). Gated by `compiler_tests/OverloadGeneric*` and `OverloadBoundNamesForced`, which accept; `XXXOverloadReturnEveryInstance` and `XXXOverloadPermutedStaticParams`, which pin the two rules' refusals; and `XXXOverloadReturnObjectDomain`, which pins row 542's. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-return-type-rule/decision-record.md` sections 1 and 2.
+- F-75 **The compiled checker checks the Return Type Rule over every instance whose domain can meet, and a positional rule: when two generic declarations in the more-specific relation declare as many static parameters of their own, those parameters agree in kind by position, and the more specific return type is a subtype of the other once the other's parameters are read as its own by position.** The equal-count scope and the comparison of kinds are the rung's choices. It builds P-45. The Return Type Rule compares every instance of the less specific declaration, except that a type parameter standing as a whole parameter type where the more specific declaration has an object type is read as its union with that object type, so that only the instances whose domain meets the object are compared; the type group's 2011 paper (`Papers/Types/`) sets aside the instances whose domain is `Bottom`. So it accepts `ident[\T\](x: T): T` beside `ident(x: Circle): Circle`, `Circle` an object, and the pair runs (row 542, fixed; F-376), and the merge of the built-in number types with their objects (P-178) brings no refusal to pairs over them. 1	# Committing and pushing
2	
3	**scratch**
4	: Files and folders that your work makes and `main` does not keep: logs, captured and raw run output, copies of tools, lists and private caches folders.
5	
6	Your brief says whether you commit and push, and on which branch. If it says nothing, commit on your current branch, and push it.
7	
8	## What to commit
9	
10	- Commit your change, its tests, your report if it is a file, and any reusable script.
11	- Commit what you write to the record, such as a ledger row, with the work that it records. A row's close follows the fix's commit (`records.md`).
12	- A probe is a task of a brief that builds a change to answer a question and does not land it. Commit its change as a patch file, with its report and programs, in the `probes/` folder that the brief names, and no edit of the original tree. If the brief names no folder, commit nothing of the probe: give the patch's path and the report in your final message.
13	- Keep scratch in your tree's `tmp/`, which is gitignored.
14	- Do not commit `.claude/worktrees/` or `.claude/agents/`, which show as untracked in a fresh clone.
15	- Keep a copyrighted PDF or deck in `research/decks/`, also gitignored. Cite it by its Wayback URL. Notes on it go in `research/extracts/`: your own summary, with brief attributed quotations.
16	- Put provenance and rationale in commit messages and reports, not in source comments.
17	- Name a model by its tier (Opus, Sonnet, Fable) in any text that you commit, commit messages included. Never write its model identifier, the API's name for the model, which starts with `claude-`.
18	
19	## How to commit
20	
21	Commit as you go, each commit in one command that names its paths:
22	
23	    git add -- <paths> && git commit -m "<message>" -- <paths>
24	
25	- The command commits only the paths that it names. Other agents may have uncommitted edits in your tree. Leave them alone.
26	- If you renamed a file with `git mv`, name its old path in `git commit` only, because `git add` refuses a path that no longer exists: `git add -- <new paths> && git commit -m "<message>" -- <new paths> <old paths>`.
27	- Never commit a copied directory, and never use `git add -A`.
28	- Before you commit more than a few hundred lines, stage them and read what you staged: `git add -- <paths> && git diff --cached --stat -- <paths>`.
29	- If the commit edits the original tree, say so in its message.
30	- End every commit message with this footer, exactly, whatever footer Claude Code suggests:
31	
32	      Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
33	      Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AmiXNpJxQ6TBwec4vJZHDB
34	
35	  If your brief gives another session line, use it. If a commit that is already made has a footer that names a model, by any name or identifier, leave the commit as it is. Such a footer is not a defect: do not check for it, report it or list it.
36	
37	## Pushing
38	
39	Push after every commit.
40	
41	- If you work on your own branch, push it: `git push -u origin <branch>` the first time, then `git push`. Your brief says how the branch reaches `main`.
42	- From a session in a cloud container, do not try to delete a branch on GitHub, or retry a refusal with another tool (the `cloud-container` skill, "Rules for every agent"). Removing a worktree leaves its branch. Ask nobody in your report to delete a branch.
43	- If you work on `main`, other agents commit to it too. Push only your own commits:
44	  1. Run `git log origin/main..main`. Your commits are those whose hashes your own `git commit` printed.
45	  2. If it lists another agent's commit, run the command again shortly: that agent pushes right after it commits. If the commit stays, push nothing, and say so in your report.
46	  3. If it lists only your commits, push the three refs with this one command, and wait for it to end:
47	
48	         git push --atomic origin main main:claude/worker-brief-fable-vnnuv8 main:blinded-fable
49	
50	     With `--atomic`, the three refs update together or not at all. Do not pipe the command into another command, since a pipe hides a refusal. A refusal shows as a line that starts with `!`, and as a non-zero exit. The platform rebuilds a lost container from `blinded-fable`.
51	- Push no branch that this section does not name, unless your brief names it.
52	- If a push is refused, push nothing more, and do not run it again. Report the refused ref and git's message.

# Climb batch 31, run 1: the judge's ruling on the red gate

The ruling is by reading only: no build, no suite and no program was run. The tree read is `main` at `280835f438`; the gate ran at `2c891b65b0`, and the three commits after it change no code (`git diff --stat 2c891b65b0..HEAD` lists `Specification/appendices/changes.tex` and files under `explorations/` only).

## Decision: repair

The gate is red on one test, `compiler_tests/XXXOverloadGenericObjectTwoParams`, an expected failure that rung X added (`1ce04203c5`). The test asserts a crash of the checker that shows or does not show by what the same JVM compiled before. No code of the batch is wrong, and no rung is dropped. The repair takes the program out of the gated folder and keeps it as the probe of its ledger row. It changes no Java, no Scala, no library file and no other test.

## The evidence

The failing case, `sed -n '180,182p;4411,4414p' ProjectFortress/TEST-RESULTS/fast-compiler/TEST-com.sun.fortress.tests.unit_tests.CompilerJUTest.txt`:

     compile /home/user/fortress/ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXOverloadGenericObjectTwoParams 
     Saw failure, but did not satisfy compile_err_contains; expected
    V is not in the kind env
    Testcase: /home/user/fortress/ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXOverloadGenericObjectTwoParams took 0.194 sec
    	FAILED
    Saw wrong failure. compile

What these lines show, by the harness's code:

- The compile printed nothing, on standard output or on standard error. The harness taps both streams (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/tests/unit_tests/FileTests.java:313-316`), and on this branch prints a line break and then releases both taps before its own message (`FileTests.java:402-404`). The line break is there, after the path; nothing stands between it and ' Saw failure'. A compile test runs in the suite's own JVM (`FileTests.java:762-765`, `Shell.subMain`), so no output went elsewhere.
- 'Saw failure' does not say that the compile failed. The branch is taken when the test should fail and either nothing failed or a key is unmet (`FileTests.java:394-408`), and it prints 'Saw failure, but did not satisfy' whenever a key is unmet (`:405-408`). The exit code is not printed. The skill's `references/tests-writing.md`, "How `XXX` works", says the same of this message: an `XXX` compile test with a `compile_err_contains` key "whose program compiles, reports 'Saw wrong failure'".

So in the gate's suite the compile did not reach the crash. It printed what a compile that succeeds prints: nothing. Whether it exited 0 is not on record.

The same file, elsewhere, reaches the crash:

- alone, seven times of seven on the merged tree (the gate's result: once at one thread, six times at four, private caches, each 'XXXOverloadGenericObjectTwoParams.fss:5:8-12: V is not in the kind env [][][]', rc 255);
- alone through the harness on rung X's tree ('Saw expected failure', `OK (1 test)`, `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-return-rule-object/REPORT.md:79`);
- in rung X's whole `ant testFast` (`REPORT.md:46-48`, `:135`), and in the gather's one JVM of the batch's 58 compiled tests on the merged tree, "each passing or seen as its expected failure" (`explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-31/RECORD.md:50`).

Two whole-suite JVMs, one green and one red, at the same thread count: what differs is the JVM's history. The suite shuffles its files (`FileTests.java:997`).

## The source

The program (`ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXOverloadGenericObjectTwoParams.fss:8-9`, `:12`) calls `keep(Duo[\Square, Square\](Square, Square))` for `keep[\T\](x: T): T` beside `keep[\U extends Object, V extends Object\](x: Duo[\U, V\]): Duo[\U, V\]`. By reading:

1. Both declarations fit the call without coercion, and at the call each has the one parameter type `Duo[\Square, Square\]`. Candidates that fit by subtyping carry no declared arrow (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/impls/Functionals.scala:919-930`, the last case), so they are compared on their instances (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/useful/STypesUtil.scala:1150-1165`, the last case), which are equal.
2. For a tie "among candidates with one parameter type" the checker "keeps the sort's head" (`Functionals.scala:1104-1108`). The sort keeps the order of its input where the order does not decide (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/useful/PartialOrder.scala:8-12`), and its input is the list of the reference's overloadings (`Functionals.scala:1587-1592`).
3. The head's static arguments are then put into every other overloading (`STypesUtil.scala:1170-1198`). Row 1046 places the crash there: the second declaration's domain, "still holding `V`", is asked against the best arrow's (`STypesUtil.scala:1195-1197`). That happens for one head and not for the other.
4. That the head of such a tie varies with the compiling JVM is measured, on another pair: the gap ledger's history, row 499, "the direct call `f(b)` on a `Box[\Blue\]` answers `box` or `any` depending on the compiling JVM (four isolated harness runs of the pair on the base's classes answered `any`; the same test in a 29-file run answered `box`)", with the same lines of the checker named (then `Functionals.scala:741-749`).

Where the order of the overloadings comes from is not traced. Which head reaches the crash is not traced either; point 3 is a reading.

Nothing of this is the batch's code: the crash stands on the base (`REPORT.md:76`, the base column), the batch changes neither `Functionals.scala` nor the lines of `STypesUtil.scala` above (`git diff --stat c1ce2a35e1..HEAD -- ProjectFortress/src` lists `OverloadSet.java`, `CodeGen.java`, `VarCodeGen.java`, `FTraitOrObject.java`, `OverloadedFunction.java`, `LabelExit.java`, `OverloadingOracle.scala` and 76 added lines of `STypesUtil.scala`), and the crash is "in the type check of the call, before the overloading check" that rung X repaired (row 1046).

## What each side had right

The gate:

The test asserts a checker crash ('V is not in the kind env') that shows or not by what the same JVM compiled before.
In the gate's suite the compile printed nothing at all; alone (7 of 7), in rung X's testFast and in the gather's JVM it crashed.
Cause by reading: the call ties two generic candidates and the checker keeps the sort's head (Functionals.scala:1104-1108); row 499's history measured that this head varies by compiling JVM.

Ruling file: /home/user/fortress/explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-31/JUDGE-gate.md, committed locally as f87a870f15, not pushed.
Four items go to the curator: the decision to hold a specification-settled defect by row and probe alone, the unscheduled tie defect, one untraced sibling test, two tool remarks.
forCurator: Decision taken where the record does not settle it: row 1046's defect is settled by the specification, and tests-writing.md's way 2 asks a gated XXX test for it, but no gated form holds while the checker's answer varies with the JVM's history; the ruling keeps the row and a probe, no gated test. Ways: (a) as ruled; cost: the defect is ungated until the tie is decided. (b) Decide the tie in the checker within this batch; cost: a checker change outside every rung's declaration on the merged tree, with its own test, count, distance and skeptic. (c) Run each compile test in a JVM of its own; cost: suite time, and the dependence stays in the checker. Reversible; does not hold the push.

The defect under it has no place in the plan by name: a call tied among generic candidates whose instances have one parameter type is resolved by the order of the overloadings, which varies with what the JVM compiled before (rows 499, 1047, 1046; ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/impls/Functionals.scala:1104-1108). The suite shuffles its files with the clock as seed (FileTests.java:1236, :1255-1257), so any gated test whose verdict hangs on that head can turn red in some order. PLAN.md:256 schedules row 499's dispatcher half only; row 499's history names the repair (compare on declared domains). The gate's ant testFast printed 'FORTRESS_UNITTESTS_SEED=1a1e78bd82d_16' twice, by reading this suite's seed (CompilerJUTest.java:42-43), so the red order may be replayable; not checked by a run.

Not ruled, not traced: ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/OverloadReturnObjectDomain.fss:26, b: Box[\Square\] = keep(Box[\Square\](Square)), is fitted by both the top-level keep[\T\] (:16) and Box[\U\]'s functional method keep(self) (:10) at Box[\Square\], and the test asserts 'keep Box'. It was green in the three suite histories on record (rung X's testFast, the gather's one JVM, the gate). Whether its verdict can vary with the head is not established by this reading.

Two tool remarks, neither red: the gate brief's atomic_runs returns 1 whenever the summary holds '# testFast: BUILD FAILED' (72 of 72 PASS here); and the harness prints 'Saw failure, but did not satisfy' also where the command did not fail, without the exit code (FileTests.java:399-408), which is why the gate could not say what the compile did.
